groups.title: Metaphysics
groups.load_bearing_use: Baseline framing for metaphysics as inquiry into being, first causes, and related core questions, plus the modern shift away from defining the field by a single subject-matter.

groups.title: Metaphysical Grounding
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports the shift from flat existence questions toward constitutive explanation and 'in-virtue-of' structure.

groups.title: Fundamentality
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports the claim that metaphysics is not only about what exists but about what is basic and how dependence is ordered.

groups.title: Essential vs. Accidental Properties
groups.load_bearing_use: Background on modal and non-modal ways of understanding essence and why a bare necessity test is often insufficient.

groups.title: Kit Fine
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports the archive's use of the Finean thought that metaphysical necessity may hold in virtue of essence rather than essence being reduced to modality.

groups.title: Metaphysical Grounding
groups.load_bearing_use: Primary source for grounding as constitutive rather than causal determination.

groups.title: Fundamentality
groups.load_bearing_use: Primary source for the idea of absolute fundamentality as ontological independence or ungroundedness, and for the dual tasks of fundamentality.

groups.title: Truthmakers
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports truthmaker discipline as one way to keep metaphysical claims answerable to being.

groups.title: Substance
groups.load_bearing_use: Background for substance ontology and bearerhood.

groups.title: Process Philosophy
groups.load_bearing_use: Pressure source for taking becoming and dynamism as metaphysically primary in at least some domains.

groups.title: Monism
groups.load_bearing_use: Pressure source for world-level unity and priority monism.

groups.title: Mereology
groups.load_bearing_use: Background on parts, wholes, and compositional structure.

groups.title: Laws of Nature
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports the contrast between laws and accidental regularities and the need for stronger grounding of lawhood.

groups.title: The Metaphysics of Causation
groups.load_bearing_use: Background for what causation is supposed to be in virtue of and for causal pluralism pressure.

groups.title: Properties
groups.load_bearing_use: Background on dispositional properties and their role in metaphysical explanation.

groups.title: Time
groups.load_bearing_use: Background on presentism, eternalism, persistence, and the structure of temporal metaphysics.

groups.title: Temporal Parts
groups.load_bearing_use: Primary source on the endurance/perdurance debate.

groups.title: Identity Over Time
groups.load_bearing_use: Background on persistence and diachronic identity conditions.

groups.title: Emergent Properties
groups.load_bearing_use: Primary source for emergence as the conjunction of dependence and autonomy.

groups.title: Scientific Reduction
groups.load_bearing_use: Background for reduction and its limits.

groups.title: Intertheory Relations in Physics
groups.load_bearing_use: Background on reduction, weak emergence, and relations between levels of theory.

groups.title: Social Ontology
groups.load_bearing_use: Primary source for social ontology as inquiry into the nature and properties of the social world and social construction.

groups.title: Ontological Dependence
groups.load_bearing_use: Background for dependence relations that are neither straightforwardly causal nor merely conceptual.

groups.title: Metaphysical Explanation
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports the archive's insistence that social and normative facts still call for metaphysical explanation rather than deflation.

groups.title: Neo-Aristotelian Metaphysics
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports treating contemporary neo-Aristotelian work as a live organizing family rather than only a historical curiosity.

groups.title: Monism
groups.load_bearing_use: Primary pressure source for existence monism and priority monism.

groups.title: Process Philosophy
groups.load_bearing_use: Primary pressure source for process-first metaphysics.

groups.title: Physicalism
groups.load_bearing_use: Pressure source for strong naturalistic reductionism.

groups.title: Possible Worlds
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports treating possible-worlds discourse as a central modal framework while leaving open competing ontologies of worlds.

groups.title: Truthmakers
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports using truthmaker pressure to keep modal and other metaphysical claims answerable to being without collapsing everything into causation.

groups.title: Essential vs. Accidental Properties
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports the essentialist strand that explains at least some modal facts by the natures of things rather than by world-talk alone.

groups.title: Material Constitution
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports the distinction between constitution and identity and the pressure from coincident-object puzzles and reality-explosion worries.

groups.title: Ordinary Objects
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports treating ordinary objects as a live metaphysical target rather than as a mere commonsense placeholder.

groups.title: Mereology
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports the disciplined separation of parthood questions from constitution, dependence, and sortal questions.

groups.title: Form vs. Matter
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports using hylomorphic or formed-whole ideas as a middle path between eliminativism and uncontrolled coincidence.

groups.title: Properties
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports treating properties as central metaphysical entities and frames the universalist side of the contemporary debate.

groups.title: Tropes
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports the role of particularized property-instances and the idea that trope theorists use them to explain concrete qualitative character.

groups.title: Relations
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports keeping relations first-class rather than treating them as a dispensable shadow of monadic properties.

groups.title: Nominalism in Metaphysics
groups.load_bearing_use: Supplies the pressure from strict nominalist and trope-nominalist alternatives, clarifying what a middle posture must answer.

groups.title: Universals
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports the classical and contemporary role of universals in explaining resemblance and qualitative recurrence.

groups.title: Identity
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports the archive's treatment of individuation and criteria of identity as explicit metaphysical burdens rather than as afterthoughts.

groups.title: Identity
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports treating strict numerical identity as a real metaphysical notion while distinguishing it from Geach-style relative identity pressures.

groups.title: Sortals
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports the claim that many identity judgments are intelligible only through kind-, count-, or matter-sensitive criteria rather than by bare numerical sameness alone.

groups.title: The Identity of Indiscernibles
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports treating discernibility as a serious metaphysical constraint while refusing to identify it straightforwardly with the ground of identity.

groups.title: Relative Identity
groups.load_bearing_use: Pressure source for cases where something may be the same F but not the same G, helping the archive distinguish strict identity from sortal-relative sameness claims.

groups.title: Haecceitism
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports treating primitive thisness as a live but costly posit, especially when worlds can differ non-qualitatively without qualitative difference.

groups.title: Ontological Dependence
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports treating ontological dependence as a family of relations and distinguishes broader dependence talk from stricter grounding talk.

groups.title: Metaphysical Grounding
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports the archive's use of grounding as constitutive rather than causal determination and explanation.

groups.title: Supervenience
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports the claim that supervenience is often too coarse-grained to replace realization or grounding and works better as a modal constraint than as a complete explanation.

groups.title: Emergent Properties
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports treating emergence debates as drawing on several different dependence relations, including composition, supervenience, realization, grounding, and causation.

groups.title: Metaphysical Explanation
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports the archive's emphasis on choosing the right explanatory relation rather than treating every metaphysical “because” as uniform.

groups.title: Existence
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports treating existence as a substantive metaphysical problem rather than as a trivial shadow of quantification or grammar.

groups.title: Ontological Commitment
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports treating ontological commitment as tied to what must exist for a theory to be true, while emphasizing that criteria of commitment vary with truth-conditional and logical assumptions.

groups.title: Logic and Ontology
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports the archive's caution that logical regimentation illuminates ontology without settling every metaphysical question by itself.

groups.title: Truthmakers
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports the archive's use of truthmaker pressure when quantifier-only bookkeeping underdescribes what reality must be like for a discourse or theory to be true.

groups.title: States of Affairs
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports treating states of affairs as structured complexes that obtain or fail to obtain and clarifies their relation to facts and modality.

groups.title: Facts
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports the distinction between facts and states of affairs, including the idea that obtaining can be a mode of being rather than mere existence-talk.

groups.title: Truthmakers
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports treating truthmaking as grounding-style answerability to reality without forcing one truthmaker object for every sentence.

groups.title: Propositions
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports treating propositions as primary bearers of truth and falsity and as sharable contents of attitudes rather than as worldly facts.

groups.title: The Correspondence Theory of Truth
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports the archive's use of correspondence-style pressure from truth to reality while keeping open multiple candidates for the relevant worldly relata.

groups.title: Abstract Objects
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports treating the abstract/concrete distinction as metaphysically significant while noting that there is no single settled way to draw it.

groups.title: Platonism in Metaphysics
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports the standard contemporary characterization of platonism as realism about abstract, non-spatiotemporal, causally inert objects.

groups.title: Philosophy of Mathematics
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports using mathematics as a central pressure point for abstract ontology and for the question of how we know or describe abstracta.

groups.title: Structuralism in the Philosophy of Mathematics
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports the archive's bias toward structural and role-based treatments of mathematical ontology rather than a brute census of abstract individuals.

groups.title: Nominalism in the Philosophy of Mathematics
groups.load_bearing_use: Keeps nominalist and fictionalist pressure visible by showing how one might aim to preserve mathematical practice without commitment to abstract mathematical objects.

groups.title: Events
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports treating events as a genuine metaphysical category distinct from facts, and highlights redescription, fine-graining, and individuation pressures.

groups.title: Events
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports the point that event theories are often chosen together with broader metaphysical commitments and foregrounds the problem of event identity conditions.

groups.title: Process Philosophy
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports treating becoming and dynamic organization as metaphysically serious without forcing the archive into a single process-only system.

groups.title: The Metaphysics of Causation
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports the claim that causal metaphysics must be sensitive to different kinds of relata, including token happenings, types, and variable-based structures.

groups.title: Absolute and Relational Space and Motion: Classical Theories
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports keeping the absolute-versus-relational pressure visible while resisting any assumption that one crude container or distance-only model settles the metaphysics of space.

groups.title: Boundary
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports treating boundaries as pervasive ontological demarcations whose exact status can vary across natural, vague, and conventional cases.

groups.title: Holes
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports using holes and other negative spatial cases as stress tests for whether spatial ontology can accommodate dependent, locatable, causally relevant absences without inflation.

groups.title: The Hole Argument
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports caution about literalist substantival readings of spacetime and underscores the risk of surplus mathematical structure in spatial ontology.

groups.title: Metaphysics of Quantum Gravity
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports keeping open the possibility that familiar spacetime structure is emergent from a more fundamental non-spatiotemporal basis.

groups.title: Natural Kinds
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports treating kindhood as a live metaphysical issue about genuinely natural classification, essences, and whether scientific groupings track worldly joints rather than mere convenience.

groups.title: Sortals
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports distinguishing kindhood and sortal discipline from mere predication, especially where counting, individuation, and kind-sensitive identity judgments matter.

groups.title: Social Ontology
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports allowing socially constructed or socially anchored categories to be metaphysically serious without either reducing them away or mistaking them for timeless natural kinds.

groups.title: Natural Properties
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports keeping naturalness as a graded and controversial feature of reality rather than assuming that one flat inventory of perfectly natural properties must monopolize all real classification.

groups.title: Artifact
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports treating artifact kinds as a genuine pressure case for functional, historical, and design-sensitive classification rather than dismissing them as purely verbal groupings.

groups.title: Teleological Notions in Biology
groups.load_bearing_use: Primary pressure source for treating function and goal-directedness as explanatory in biology while distinguishing immanent teleology from crude design analogies.

groups.title: Aristotle on Causality
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports the irreducibility and explanatory role of final causation within a plural causal framework rather than a purely efficient-causal picture.

groups.title: Aristotle's Biology
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports the link between form, life-function, and organized development in living beings, which helps keep teleology tied to structure rather than detached sloganizing.

groups.title: Causal Role Theories of Functional Explanation
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports the distinction between etiological and causal-role accounts of function and the broader thought that functional explanation can be legitimate in both natural and social domains.

groups.title: Consciousness
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports treating consciousness as a central issue about mind and its place in nature rather than as a dispensable remainder.

groups.title: Self-Consciousness
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports distinguishing consciousness from self-consciousness and treating first-person reference and ownership as load-bearing rather than decorative.

groups.title: Phenomenological Approaches to Self-Consciousness
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports the thought that experience has an intrinsic first-personal or prereflective self-givenness without requiring reflective introspection.

groups.title: Personal Identity
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports separating personhood and persistence questions from more minimal questions about consciousness and subjecthood.

groups.title: Panpsychism
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports treating panpsychism as a live pressure source against reductionism while refusing to let it win by default.

groups.title: Agency
groups.load_bearing_use: Primary source for agency as the capacity to act, for the standard intentional-action conception, and for the pressure from initiation- and agency-first alternatives.

groups.title: Action
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports the distinction between action and mere movement, the role of primary reasons in action explanation, and the link between rationalizing and causal explanations.

groups.title: Free Will
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports the treatment of free will as significant control over action and the distinction between freedom-to-do-otherwise and sourcehood/self-determination.

groups.title: Personal Autonomy
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports the archive's treatment of self-government as real but vulnerable, and of manipulation, addiction, coercion, and reasons-responsiveness as tests of agential control.

groups.title: Moral Responsibility
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports distinguishing agency from the stronger powers and capacities required for full responsibility while keeping answerability connected to agential control.

groups.title: Reasons for Action: Justification, Motivation, Explanation
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports treating reasons as genuine guides and explanations of action without collapsing justifying, motivating, and explanatory roles into one.

groups.title: Life
groups.load_bearing_use: Primary source for the metaphysical and definitional pressure around life itself, including skepticism about one simple essence-of-life formula and the need to distinguish different explanatory goals.

groups.title: Biological Individuals
groups.load_bearing_use: Primary source for organisms as paradigm biological individuals, and for the pressure from autonomy, integration, shared fate, and symbiosis on criteria of organismic individuality.

groups.title: Philosophy of Cell Biology
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports the archive’s emphasis on living autonomy as organized control and self-maintenance rather than as a mysterious extra force.

groups.title: Levels of Organization in Biology
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports the archive’s plural, multi-level treatment of living organization and warns against forcing every biological explanation into one privileged scale.

groups.title: Teleological Notions in Biology
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports the claim that biological teleology is hard to eliminate and helps connect organismic form, function, and directedness without collapsing them into external design.

groups.title: Aristotle’s Metaphysics
groups.load_bearing_use: Primary source for the priority, intelligibility, and teleological role of actuality relative to potentiality, and for the claim that becoming is not exhausted by a flat inventory of present actual states.

groups.title: Aristotle’s Natural Philosophy
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports the archive’s treatment of change as the actualization of structured potentiality, and of active/passive powers as linked to causation and form rather than to bare possibility.

groups.title: Dispositions
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports the continuity between potentiality-talk, powers, capacities, tendencies, and disposition theory in contemporary metaphysics.

groups.title: Abilities
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports the note’s treatment of agential potentials as real powers whose exercise depends on obstacles, circumstances, and organized control rather than on crude possible-world bookkeeping alone.

groups.title: Form vs. Matter
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports the archive’s insistence that potentiality and actuality are tied to form, organization, and hylomorphic structure rather than floated as free-standing modal residues.

groups.title: Holes
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports treating holes as a paradigmatic case where ordinary ontology, causal talk, and quantification put pressure on a positivity-only metaphysics.

groups.title: Truthmakers
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports the pressure from negative and universal truths, and why truthmaker discipline cannot simply ignore them.

groups.title: States of Affairs
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports distinguishing facts, obtaining/non-obtaining states of affairs, and truth-bearers so absence talk is not flattened into one category.

groups.title: The Metaphysics of Causation
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports treating omission and absence cases as a live pressure point in causal metaphysics rather than as a settled pseudo-problem.

groups.title: The Metaphysics of Nothing
groups.load_bearing_use: Supplies wider background on the presence/absence distinction and on why absence should not be conflated with absolute nothingness.

groups.title: Intentionality
groups.load_bearing_use: Primary source for intentionality as aboutness or directedness, and for the pressure against treating contentful mentality as a mere linguistic gloss.

groups.title: Mental Representation
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports distinguishing representation from mere causation while keeping teleological, functional, inferential, and externalist approaches visible as live explanatory strategies.

groups.title: Consciousness and Intentionality
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports keeping the relation between phenomenal consciousness and aboutness explicit rather than silently assuming either identity or complete independence.

groups.title: Collective Intentionality
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports treating jointly directed attitudes and socially scaffolded intentionality as live metaphysical possibilities rather than mere metaphors.

groups.title: Intentionality (IEP)
groups.load_bearing_use: Supplies broader background on aboutness across thought and language, including the pressure from empty or non-veridical intentional states.

groups.title: Form vs. Matter
groups.load_bearing_use: Primary pressure source for treating hylomorphism as a live contemporary option and for distinguishing form from mere shape and matter from brute stuff-talk.

groups.title: Aristotle's Metaphysics
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports the link between form, substance, and essence, and helps anchor the thought that hylomorphic compounds are intelligible through more than material inventory alone.

groups.title: Aristotle's Natural Philosophy
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports the archive’s emphasis on material constraints and hypothetical necessity, keeping form tied to realization conditions rather than treating it as a free-floating principle.

groups.title: Object
groups.load_bearing_use: Supplies contemporary metaphysical pressure for using hylomorphism to explain organized objects, structure, and kindhood without collapsing wholes into bare part-sums.

groups.title: Substance
groups.load_bearing_use: Provides broader background on substance and hylomorphism, including the link between material substances and matter-form composition in the Aristotelian tradition.

groups.title: Nonexistent Objects
groups.load_bearing_use: Primary source for the core pressure that thought and discourse target Pegasus-, Vulcan-, and Sherlock-style cases without thereby settling whether there are corresponding nonexistent objects.

groups.title: Fictional Entities
groups.load_bearing_use: Primary source for the ontological options surrounding fictional characters and places, and for the need to distinguish discourse about fiction from ordinary concrete ontology.

groups.title: Possible Objects
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports the note’s caution that merely possible-object talk can be useful without automatically requiring a populated ontology of unreal residents.

groups.title: Impossible Worlds
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports treating impossible contents and contradictory fictions as a real pressure point on representation and semantics without immediately licensing unrestricted impossible-object ontology.

groups.title: Intentionality
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports the note’s starting claim that aboutness or directedness can exceed successful reference and present contact, which is the main pressure behind merely intentional being.

groups.title: Monism
groups.load_bearing_use: Primary source for distinguishing existence monism from priority monism and for the pressure that the maximal concrete whole might be prior to its proper parts.

groups.title: Mereology
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports disciplined talk about part, whole, maximality, and composition so worldhood is not reduced to a vague list of everything.

groups.title: Fundamentality
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports the distinction between what exists and what is basic, which is essential for keeping cosmic priority separate from existence monism.

groups.title: Truthmakers
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports the note's treatment of totality and completeness conditions, especially the pressure around totality facts and the temptation to reify every limit-clause.

groups.title: Possible Worlds
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports keeping modal world-talk distinct from the ontology of the actual concrete world-whole, while preserving the idea of a world as a maximal connected whole in some frameworks.

groups.title: Causal Determinism
groups.load_bearing_use: Primary pressure source for the thought that every event might be necessitated by antecedent conditions plus laws, which the note needs in order to distinguish deterministic closure from contingency and objective chance.

groups.title: Chance versus Randomness
groups.load_bearing_use: Primary source for separating chance from randomness, unpredictability, and mere ignorance, and for keeping objective chance conceptually distinct from subjective uncertainty.

groups.title: Interpretations of Probability
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports the note’s insistence that not all probability talk is of one kind and that metaphysical work is needed to distinguish credence, evidential probability, and objective chance.

groups.title: Future Contingents
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports the note’s treatment of not-yet-settled futures and the pressure to explain how future-directed truths differ from necessities and inevitabilities.

groups.title: Branching Time
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports the note’s claim that open futurity can be modeled or understood through branching structures without automatically settling a maximally inflated ontology of concrete branches.

groups.title: Principle of Sufficient Reason
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports the note’s refusal to identify contingency with unintelligibility, since the pressure for sufficient reason remains even where necessity fails.

groups.title: Intrinsic vs. Extrinsic Properties
groups.load_bearing_use: Primary source for the distinction between intrinsic and extrinsic properties, the warning that several distinctions are being run together, and the taxonomy separating local/non-local, interior/exterior, and duplication-preserving notions.

groups.title: Natural Properties
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports the connection between naturalness, duplication, intrinsicness, similarity, lawhood, and explanatory joint-carving without requiring naturalness to settle every ontological issue.

groups.title: David Lewis’s Metaphysics
groups.load_bearing_use: Provides the background picture of Humean supervenience, perfectly natural properties, and the Lewisian use of duplication in theorizing about intrinsic character.

groups.title: Relations
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports the internal/external relation distinction and the idea that some relations supervene on the intrinsic natures of relata while others depend on broader composites or surroundings.

groups.title: Holism and Nonseparability in Physics
groups.load_bearing_use: Supplies pressure against mosaic absolutism by showing that physical holism and nonseparability remain live where some qualitative intrinsic physical properties or relations fail to supervene on local intrinsic bases.

groups.title: Vagueness
groups.load_bearing_use: Provides the baseline characterization of vagueness through borderline cases, inquiry resistance, higher-order vagueness, and the live dispute over whether all vagueness is linguistic rather than worldly.

groups.title: The Problem of the Many
groups.load_bearing_use: Supplies the core ontological pressure from clouds and other boundary-indeterminate cases, showing why vagueness is not only about predicates but also about composition, counting, and ordinary objecthood.

groups.title: Ordinary Objects
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports the claim that puzzles about ordinary objects repeatedly force a choice among overpopulation, arbitrariness, and indeterminacy, which is exactly why the archive needs a disciplined stance on vague being and borderline ontology.

groups.title: Material Constitution
groups.load_bearing_use: Keeps visible the way constitution and composition disputes invite eliminative, plenitudinous, and sometimes vagueness-based responses, helping the archive connect borderline cases to formed wholes rather than treating vagueness as a standalone language puzzle.

groups.title: Object
groups.load_bearing_use: Primary pressure source for bundle theory, bare particularism, and hylomorphism as rival accounts of what concrete objects are, including the idea that objects may be bundles of coinstantiated universals or compresent tropes, or instead include a bare particular or form-matter structure.

groups.title: Substance
groups.load_bearing_use: Primary source for the distinction between substance as object-like being and substance as fundamental being, and for the contemporary controversy between bundle theories, thin particulars, substrata, and hylomorphic views.

groups.title: Tropes
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports the trope-bundle side of the debate by treating tropes as particularized property-instances and by situating trope bundle theory as a live way of construing concrete particulars without universals or substrata.

groups.title: Substance
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports the note’s three-way distinction between object-like substances, fundamental substances, and substrata, and helps keep bearerhood separate from both bare material stuff and deepest fundamentality.

groups.title: Plural Quantification
groups.load_bearing_use: Primary pressure source for the claim that true plural discourse need not automatically add a further object to ontology, and for the idea that plural reference can sometimes resist reification into sets or complex objects.

groups.title: Mereology
groups.load_bearing_use: Primary source for parthood, sums, and fusion, and for the thought that there is a distinct metaphysical question whether some things compose one further whole.

groups.title: Ordinary Objects
groups.load_bearing_use: Supplies live pressure from composition arguments pushing toward universalism or nihilism, which matters for distinguishing genuine wholes from arbitrary pluralities and aggregates.

groups.title: Abstract Objects
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports the note’s insistence that sets are paradigmatically abstract candidates and should not simply be identified with concrete collections, aggregates, or grouped materials.

groups.title: Social Ontology
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports the distinction between mere member-collections and socially organized collective beings whose persistence and identity depend on roles, practices, institutions, and constructed structure rather than on extensional sameness alone.

groups.title: Personal Identity
groups.load_bearing_use: Supplies the core distinction between questions about ourselves as persons and questions about ourselves as living things, conscious beings, moral agents, or material objects, which is exactly the category-separation this note needs.

groups.title: Animalism
groups.load_bearing_use: Keeps live the pressure that we may be human animals and that personhood may be a temporary property rather than our whole essence, sharpening the note’s distinction between organismic persistence and person-level unity.

groups.title: Self-Consciousness
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports the claim that self-consciousness is deeply connected with personhood and rationality while not simply being identical with consciousness in general.

groups.title: Phenomenological Approaches to Self-Consciousness
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports the note’s insistence that minimal selfhood or prereflective self-awareness can be structurally present prior to explicit autobiography, mirror-recognition, or narrative articulation.

groups.title: Personal Autonomy
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports the treatment of persons as practically integrated and self-governing beings whose agency can be real yet vulnerable to coercion, manipulation, fragmentation, and dependency.

groups.title: Paul Ricoeur
groups.load_bearing_use: Supplies pressure from narrative identity and practical-historical selfhood, helping the note distinguish between minimal selfhood and thicker person-level unity without reducing the person to a mere story.

groups.title: Mental Causation
groups.load_bearing_use: Primary pressure source for preserving genuine mental causation without sliding either into interaction mystery or epiphenomenal irrelevance.

groups.title: Physicalism
groups.load_bearing_use: Pressure source for strong reductive and supervenience-based mind-body pictures and for the exclusion-style difficulties that motivate non-reductive refinement.

groups.title: Dualism
groups.load_bearing_use: Pressure source for preserving mental distinctness while exposing the costs of external mind-body bifurcation and interaction puzzles.

groups.title: Emergent Properties
groups.load_bearing_use: Supports the archive’s use of emergence as dependence-plus-autonomy in psychophysical cases where organization matters.

groups.title: Anomalous Monism
groups.load_bearing_use: Keeps open the distinction between token unity and type-level reduction, and provides a live model of non-reductive monism under pressure from epiphenomenal worries.
